Level P1

Terminal Access: Stacks & Queues

Master LIFO and FIFO correctly to hack the system

What You'll Learn

1 Implement a Stack (LIFO) with push/pop
2 Implement a Queue (FIFO) with enqueue/dequeue
3 Use collections.deque for efficiency
4 Handle empty structure edge cases

Key Terms

Term Definition
LIFO Last In, First Out (Stack). Like a stack of plates.
FIFO First In, First Out (Queue). Like a line at a store.
Push/Pop Add to / Remove from the top of a Stack.
Enqueue/Dequeue Add to the back / Remove from the front of a Queue.

Data Structures

Structure Guide

Implement these two classes in student/data_structs.py.

1 Stack Implementation
Use a Python list. The end of the list is the "top" of the stack.
  • push: append(item)
  • pop: pop() (removes from end)
  • peek: return list[-1]
  • Check for empty before popping/peeking! Return None if empty.
2 Queue Implementation
Use collections.deque for efficiency.
  • Import: from collections import deque
  • Init: self._items = deque()
  • enqueue: append(item)
  • dequeue: popleft() (removes from front)
  • front: return deque[0]
  • Check for empty! Return None if empty.

Your Mission

Hack the Terminal

The Control Hub terminal is locked. It expects commands to be processed in reverse (Stack) and in order (Queue).

Implement the data structures to pass the system checks and unlock the door.
